To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have demonstrated a high-performance 64 GHz transmit-receive phased-array link using a 32-element SiGepatch array with a data rate of 2 Gbps at 300 m and a system noise figure < 8 dB.
the 64 GHz transmit-receive link achieves a data rate of 1 Gbit/s at 300 m, and 4 Gbit/s at shorter distances, with 32 antenna elements, using 16-Qam modulation.
a 2 Gbps communication link is demonstrated between two 32-antenna arrays at 64 GHz.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and implementation of a 64 GHz 300 meter range transmit/receive phased array link.
the development of high data rate wireless communication links in SiGe.
the design and analysis of a 64 GHz 32-element Si-based phased array for high data rate communications.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the presented 64 GHz communication link demonstrates a data rate of 2 Gbps at 300 m, which is the first such result for a phased array system at such a high frequency.
this work is the first to demonstrate a 64 GHz 300-meter-range, 1.6 Gbps transmit/receiver phased-array communication link.
the system demonstrates 64 GHz communication link with 1 Gbps data rate over 300 m.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the 64 GHz phased-array communication system has a very high data rate and a very long communication range, which are the two main requirements in a wireless communication system.
the 64 GHz phased arrays have been demonstrated with a high data throughput and a very large coverage.
we have demonstrated the world's first SiGe-based 64 GHz 32-element phased array for high-speed data communications.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the SiGe technology has the potential for a cost-effective, low power and high performance 5G communication link.
the SiGe phased arrays can be used for mmWave communications with high data rates and high coverage.
